Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — Oliver and I appreciated the walkthrough of Dedicated and the latency/cost controls. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups we need to qualify pricing: 

- Workload: user-facing assistant doing RAG + summarization. Model family: planning to use an 8k-context open LLM (fine-tuned variant).
- Expected volumes: ~50M tokens/day (peak days), average ~30M tokens/day. Monthly run-rate estimate ~900M tokens.
- Typical request: average prompt + context ~850 tokens, completion ~250 tokens.
- Concurrency/throughput: target 80 concurrent active sessions, with SLO ~300ms p99 latency on short completions (<=300 tokens).
- Budget: rough range $25k–$45k/month. Target unit economics: ideally <= $10 per 1M tokens (we know this depends on model & config).

Ask: Can you share a Dedicated sizing + pricing sketch (GPU type recommendation, how many reserved GPUs, expected aggregated throughput, and a $/1M token estimate at our volumes)? Also any minimum commit term you recommend for a reserved pool?

If helpful, we can loop in our infra lead (Oliver) for network/VPC requirements. Thanks — would like a ballpark before we escalate to procurement.

Cheers,
Katie

Thanks Marissa — looping in the sizing details. Hi Katie — quick note from the SE side with conservative estimates so procurement has a realistic baseline.

Assumptions: 8k-context open model (quantized 3/4 bits), continuous batching enabled, average request ~1,100 tokens, completion ~250 tokens.

Recommendation (ballpark):
- GPU type: H100 (preferred) for headroom on concurrency and lower p99 latency with our kernel optimizations; A100 80GB is viable if budget is tighter but expect ~15–20% lower throughput.
- Reserved pool size: start with 4 x H100 (80GB) for sustained traffic. This configuration provides ~35–45k tokens/sec aggregated (depending on batching characteristics) which should support ~80 concurrent active sessions with p95/p99 latencies in the 200–350ms range for shorter completions.
- Burst strategy: Add autoscaling margin or 1–2 warm GPUs in a dedicated burst pool if you expect sudden spikes beyond the sustained commit.

Pricing sketch (indicative):
- 4 x H100 reserved monthly commit: $32,000/month (includes runtime + 24/7 support + basic optimization tuning).
- Equivalent A100 pool (4 x A100): ~$27,000/month.
- This maps to an approximate unit cost at 900M tokens/month: H100 pool => ~$35.6 per 1M tokens; A100 pool => ~$30 per 1M tokens.

Notes on unit economics: your target of <= $10/1M is aggressive for a fully reserved Dedicated GPU pool at these volumes and model sizes. Typical strategies to reduce $/1M include: more aggressive quantization (if quality allows), batching & prefix caching (we can save tokens with context caching), or routing cold traffic to a hosted (cheaper) fallback for non-latency-critical requests. If you can shift some workloads to mixed-mode (hosted for lower SLO requests, Dedicated for low-latency paths) we can approach much lower effective $/1M across the whole product surface.

Commit terms: Monthly reserved is possible, but annual commit gets ~10–20% discount depending on term and support level. We can prepare both quotes.

I'll follow up with an internal perf report (tokens/sec per GPU ranges we observe in production for the same model family) and a sample canary rollout plan to validate before full commit.

Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[internal note: If they need < $15/1M, propose hybrid routing + hosted backup. Marcus to draft pricing options for Marissa to include in quote.]
